function.name: get_unread_mail
function.description: Fetch unread emails from the user's inbox. Returns subject, sender, preview, received time, and message_id for each email. Use for 'any new mail?', 'check my inbox', morning briefings, or before replying/flagging. For targeted searches by sender, subject, or date range, use search_mail instead.

top.description: Max number of emails to return (default 25, increase if user asks for more)

function.name: search_mail
function.description: Search emails using KQL (Keyword Query Language) syntax. Supports powerful queries like: "from:john subject:report", "hasAttachment:true subject:invoice", "received:2026-03-01..2026-03-19", "body:quarterly review", "from:ceo importance:high". Use this for targeted email searches instead of just listing unread mail.

function.name: list_mail_by_category
function.description: List emails tagged with a specific Outlook color category (e.g. "Follow Up", "Red Category"). Use this instead of search_mail when filtering by category — search_mail KQL does not support category filtering reliably.

category.description: Exact Outlook category name, e.g. "Follow Up"

function.name: send_mail
function.description: Compose and SEND a new email immediately. Use when the user says 'send an email to X', 'write an email to Y about Z', or 'email everyone on the project team'. If the user asks for a DRAFT, or to write something for them to review first, use create_draft instead. For replying to a received email (staying in-thread), use reply_to_mail instead. For sending to multiple recipients, pass all addresses in to. To ATTACH a OneDrive file (e.g. "send Jordan the Q2 report"): first call search_onedrive to get the file's item_id (and drive_id for SharePoint), then pass them in attachments — the tool downloads + attaches automatically.

attachments.description: OneDrive/SharePoint files to attach. Each entry is the file's item_id (and drive_id if from SharePoint) from a search_onedrive result.

function.name: reply_to_mail
function.description: Reply to an existing email and SEND it immediately, keeping the conversation in-thread. Use when the user says 'reply to that email', 'respond to Sarah's message', 'write back to John about the invoice'. Call get_unread_mail or search_mail first to get the message_id. Always reply in-thread — do NOT use send_mail to respond to a received email. If the user asks for a DRAFT, or to write something for them to review first, use create_draft instead: this tool sends.

message_id.description: ID of the email message to reply to

recipient_email.description: Email address of the recipient (include so it appears in your confirmation)

function.name: create_draft
function.description: Save an email to the user's Outlook Drafts folder WITHOUT sending it. Use when the user says 'draft a reply', 'draft an email', 'write something I can review', or 'prepare a response'. To draft a reply in-thread, pass reply_to_message_id (from get_unread_mail or search_mail) and the reply text in body; the recipient and subject come from the original. For a new email, pass to, subject and body. Returns the draft_id; if the user later says 'send it', call send_draft with that id.

reply_to_message_id.description: ID of the received email to draft a reply to (omit for a new email)

function.name: send_draft
function.description: Send a draft saved earlier with create_draft. Use when the user approves a draft: 'send it', 'looks good, send', 'go ahead'. Pass the draft_id from create_draft's result.

function.name: forward_mail
function.description: Forward an existing email to one or more recipients. Use when the user says 'forward that to X', 'send this email to the team', 'loop in Y on this thread'. Requires the original message_id — get it from get_unread_mail or search_mail first. An optional comment is prepended to the forwarded message.

message_id.description: ID of the email message to forward

to.description: Recipient email addresses to forward to

comment.description: Optional comment to include with the forwarded email

function.name: update_mail_flags
function.description: Mark an email as read/unread, flag/unflag it, or set Outlook color categories. Safe to call without user confirmation.

is_read.description: Set to true to mark as read, false for unread

categories.description: Outlook color categories to assign, e.g. ["Follow Up", "Red Category"]. Replaces all existing categories on the message.

function.name: get_mail_attachments
function.description: List the attachments on an email message. Returns attachment id, name, contentType, and size. Use before read_attachment to get the attachment IDs. Requires message_id from get_unread_mail, search_mail, or get_mail_thread.

function.name: read_attachment
function.description: Read the content of an email attachment. Supports: images (GPT-4o vision analysis), plain text/CSV (decoded), PDF (text extraction), Word .docx (text extraction). Always call get_mail_attachments first to get the attachment_id.

attachment_id.description: ID of the specific attachment (from get_mail_attachments)

function.name: get_calendar_events
function.description: Fetch calendar events within a date range. Returns event id, subject, start/end times, location, attendees, and online meeting join link if any. Use for 'what's on my calendar', 'any meetings today', 'what's my week look like', or before creating events to check for conflicts. Default to today + the next few days if no range is specified.

function.name: create_event
function.description: Create a new calendar event, meeting, or appointment. Use when the user says 'schedule a meeting', 'block time on my calendar', 'set up a call with X'. Set is_online to true to generate a Teams video meeting link. Attendees receive an invitation email. Returns the created event including the join URL if online.

start.description: Start datetime in the user's LOCAL time, as a naive ISO 8601 with NO "Z"/offset (e.g. "2026-03-20T10:00:00"). Do NOT convert to UTC.

end.description: End datetime in the user's LOCAL time, naive ISO 8601 with NO "Z" (e.g. "2026-03-20T11:00:00"). Do NOT convert to UTC.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone (e.g. "America/New_York"). Defaults to the user's own timezone — only set this if the user explicitly names a DIFFERENT zone.

is_online.description: Set to true to create a Teams meeting link for this event

function.name: update_event
function.description: Update an existing calendar event (change time, location, add attendees, etc.). Attendees may receive update notifications.

event_id.description: ID of the event to update

time_zone.description: IANA time zone; defaults to the user's own timezone. Pass start/end as the user's LOCAL time (no "Z").

attendees.description: Email addresses of attendees to set on the event (replaces existing list)

function.name: delete_event
function.description: Delete/cancel a calendar event. Attendees will be notified of the cancellation.

event_id.description: ID of the event to delete

function.name: respond_to_event
function.description: Accept, tentatively accept, or decline a calendar event invitation. Use when the user says 'accept that meeting invite', 'decline the 3pm call', 'tentatively accept the team lunch'. Requires the event_id — get it from get_calendar_events first. Sends a response to the organizer.

event_id.description: ID of the event to respond to

comment.description: Optional comment to include with the response

function.name: find_meeting_times
function.description: Find available meeting times for a group of attendees. Returns suggested time slots when all (or most) attendees are free. Useful when scheduling a meeting and you need to find a good time.

duration.description: Meeting duration in ISO 8601 format (e.g. "PT30M" for 30 min, "PT1H" for 1 hour). Default: PT1H

start.description: Start of the search window (ISO 8601). Only look for times after this.

end.description: End of the search window (ISO 8601). Only look for times before this.

time_zone.description: Time zone for the constraint window (default: UTC)

function.name: get_free_busy
function.description: Check the free/busy schedule for one or more people to find meeting availability. Use for "find a time for me and Priya and Tom", "is Sarah free Thursday afternoon?", "when is everyone available this week?". Returns busy blocks for each person in the requested window. Tip: get their email addresses from search_contacts first if you don't already have them.

emails.description: List of email addresses to check (include the signed-in user's email too if relevant)

start_time.description: Start of the window in ISO 8601 format (e.g. "2026-04-07T09:00:00")

end_time.description: End of the window in ISO 8601 format (e.g. "2026-04-07T17:00:00")

interval_minutes.description: Slot granularity in minutes (default 30). Use 15 for finer resolution.

function.name: get_teams_channel_messages
function.description: Read recent messages from a Microsoft Teams channel. Returns message content, sender, and timestamp. Use when the user asks 'what's been said in #general', 'catch me up on the engineering channel', 'what did the team say about X in Teams'. Call list_my_teams and list_team_channels first if you don't have the channel ID.

function.name: list_chats
function.description: List the user's Teams chats: 1:1 DMs, group chats, and meeting chats. Returns chat_id, type, topic or member names, and last activity. Call this first to find a chat before reading its messages.

function.name: get_chat_messages
function.description: Read recent messages from a Teams chat (1:1 DM, group chat, or meeting chat). Call list_chats first to get the chat_id.

function.name: get_meeting_transcript
function.description: Fetch the full transcript of a recorded Teams meeting. Returns speaker turns with timestamps. Use when the user asks 'what was discussed in the meeting', 'summarize the standup', 'what did Sarah say on the call'. Pass the calendar event_id (from get_calendar_events) — this tool resolves the online meeting and its transcript itself. Only meetings the signed-in user organized, recorded with transcription on, have a transcript.

event_id.description: Calendar event id from get_calendar_events (the event that has the online meeting). Not the meeting title.

function.name: send_teams_channel_message
function.description: Post a message to a Microsoft Teams channel, visible to all channel members. Use when the user says 'post to the team', 'send a message to #general', 'announce X in the engineering channel'. Call list_my_teams and list_team_channels first to get team_id and channel_id. For 1:1 or group DMs, use send_teams_chat_message instead.

function.name: send_teams_chat_message
function.description: Send a message in a Teams 1:1 DM or group chat. Use when the user says 'message Sarah directly', 'send a DM to X', 'write in the group chat'. Call list_chats first to get the chat_id. For posting to a channel (not a DM), use send_teams_channel_message instead.

chat_id.description: Teams chat ID (1:1 or group chat)

function.name: read_teams_image
function.description: Download and analyze an image shared in a Teams message using GPT-4o vision. Use when a Teams message contains an image and the user asks what it shows. The content_url comes from the attachments array in a Teams message (from get_chat_messages or get_teams_channel_messages). Only works for hosted content URLs (graph.microsoft.com paths) — not external image links.

content_url.description: The hosted content URL from the Teams message attachment (e.g. /teams/.../hostedContents/.../$value)

content_type.description: MIME type of the image (e.g. image/jpeg, image/png). Defaults to image/jpeg if unknown.

function.name: get_sharepoint_files
function.description: List files in a SharePoint document library. Returns id and driveId for each file — pass both to read_onedrive_file to read file content. Provide group_id (Teams group) OR site_id (from list_sharepoint_sites). drive_id is optional — auto-discovered if omitted.

group_id.description: Microsoft 365 group ID (Teams team ID) — auto-discovers site and drive

site_id.description: SharePoint site ID as returned by list_sharepoint_sites — drive auto-discovered

drive_id.description: Document library drive ID (optional — auto-discovered if omitted)

function.name: list_sharepoint_sites
function.description: List SharePoint sites the user has access to via their group memberships. Returns id, name, webUrl for each site. Pass the returned id as site_id to get_sharepoint_files to browse that site's files.

function.name: get_file_versions
function.description: List version history for a file in OneDrive or SharePoint. Returns each saved version with its date, size, and who modified it. Use when the user asks to see version history, restore a previous version, or find out what changed.

item_id.description: OneDrive or SharePoint file item ID

function.name: get_file_permissions
function.description: Get the list of people and links that have access to a file in OneDrive or SharePoint. Use when the user asks who can see a file, who has access, or to audit sharing.

item_id.description: OneDrive or SharePoint file item ID

function.name: list_contacts
function.description: List all contacts from the user's Outlook address book, sorted alphabetically. Returns display name, email, phone, company, and job title. Use for browsing contacts or before creating/updating one. For finding a specific person by name, use search_contacts instead.

top.description: Max number of contacts to return (default 25)

function.name: search_contacts
function.description: Search the user's Outlook contacts by name or email prefix. Returns matching contacts with email, phone, and job title. Use when you need someone's email address, or when the user asks 'do I have a contact for X'. Faster than list_contacts for looking up a specific person.

query.description: Search term — matches the beginning of display name or email address

function.name: create_contact
function.description: Create a new contact in a user's address book. At minimum provide a display name or given/surname.

function.name: update_contact
function.description: Update an existing contact in a user's address book. Use search_contacts first to find the contact ID. Only fields you provide are changed — others are left as-is.

contact_id.description: The contact ID to update (from search_contacts or list_contacts)

function.name: list_todo_task_lists
function.description: List all Microsoft To Do task lists (e.g. 'Tasks', 'Work', 'Shopping', custom lists). Returns list IDs and names. Call this first to discover list IDs before calling list_todo_tasks, or when the user asks 'what task lists do I have?'. Required before creating a task in a named list.

function.name: list_todo_tasks
function.description: List tasks in a Microsoft To Do task list. Returns task title, status (notStarted/inProgress/completed), due date, importance, and task_id. Use for 'what tasks do I have?', 'show my to-do list', or before updating/deleting a task to get the task_id. Call list_todo_task_lists first to get the list_id if needed.

task_list_id.description: ID of the To Do task list

function.name: list_my_teams
function.description: List all Microsoft Teams the current user is a member of. Returns team names and group IDs needed for Planner, SharePoint, and channel tools.

function.name: list_team_channels
function.description: List all channels in a Microsoft Teams team. Use this after list_my_teams to find the channel ID needed for reading or posting to a specific channel.

function.name: list_planner_plans
function.description: List Planner plans for a Microsoft 365 group (team). Use a team/group ID to discover available plans.

group_id.description: Microsoft 365 group ID (same as Teams team ID)

function.name: list_planner_tasks
function.description: List tasks in a Planner plan. Call list_planner_plans first to get plan IDs. Returns task titles, completion percentage, priority, and due dates.

function.name: create_todo_task
function.description: Create a new personal task in Microsoft To Do. Use this for individual tasks, personal follow-ups, reminders, and work items that belong to the user alone — e.g. 'add a task to call the dentist', 'remind me to review the proposal', 'create a task: follow up with Sarah'. This is the DEFAULT for all task creation unless the request involves a team board, Planner plan, sprint, or assigning to another person. list_id is optional — omit to use the default list automatically.

list_id.description: ID of the To Do task list. Omit to use the default list automatically.

reminder_datetime.description: When to remind the user (ISO 8601). Sets a push notification via Microsoft To Do/Outlook.

function.name: update_todo_task
function.description: Update an existing Microsoft To Do task (change title, status, due date, importance, or body).

list_id.description: ID of the To Do task list

task_id.description: ID of the task to update

function.name: delete_todo_task
function.description: Permanently delete a task from Microsoft To Do. Use when the user says 'delete that task', 'remove it from my list', 'scratch that task'. Requires list_id and task_id — call list_todo_tasks first to get them. Cannot be undone. To complete a task instead of deleting, use update_todo_task with status='completed'.

list_id.description: ID of the To Do task list

task_id.description: ID of the task to delete

function.name: create_planner_plan
function.description: Create a new Planner board (plan) for a Microsoft 365 group (team). Only needed if no plan exists yet.

function.name: create_planner_task
function.description: Create a task on a Microsoft Planner board (team task board). Use this ONLY when: the request explicitly names a Planner plan or board ('add to the sprint board', 'add to the Q2 plan', 'put on the engineering board'), OR the task is being assigned to another person ('assign this to John', 'for Sarah to complete'), OR the user says 'team task' or 'project board'. For all other task creation, use create_todo_task. Call list_my_teams then list_planner_plans first to get the plan_id.

bucket_id.description: Bucket ID to place the task in (optional)

assignments.description: Assignments object — keys are user IDs, values are { "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.plannerAssignment", "orderHint": " !" }

function.name: update_planner_task
function.description: Update an existing Planner task (change title, completion, priority, dates, or bucket). Etag is handled automatically.

bucket_id.description: Move task to a different bucket

function.name: list_onenote_notebooks
function.description: List the user's OneNote notebooks, sorted by most recently modified. Returns notebook IDs and names. Call this first when the user asks about notes or wants to find something in OneNote. Follow with list_onenote_sections to go deeper.

function.name: list_onenote_sections
function.description: List sections in a OneNote notebook. Call list_onenote_notebooks first to get notebook IDs.

function.name: list_onenote_pages
function.description: List pages in a OneNote section, sorted by most recently modified. Call list_onenote_sections first to get section IDs.

function.name: get_onenote_page_content
function.description: Get the HTML content of a specific OneNote notebook page. Only for pages in OneNote — NOT for .txt or .docx files on OneDrive/SharePoint (use read_onedrive_file for those). Call list_onenote_pages first to get page IDs.

function.name: search_onedrive
function.description: Find a file or document in OneDrive or SharePoint by name or keyword — e.g. 'find my Q3 budget', 'where is the contract doc', 'locate the design spec'. Use this whenever the user asks to find, locate, or search for a file. Returns metadata (id, name, webUrl) — NOT file content. To read a file's content after finding it, call read_onedrive_file with the item's id.

query.description: Search query — matches file names and indexed content

function.name: get_onedrive_item
function.description: Get metadata for a specific file or folder in a user's OneDrive by its path (e.g. 'Documents/report.docx')

path.description: Path relative to the OneDrive root (e.g. "Documents/report.docx")

function.name: read_onedrive_file
function.description: Read the text content of a OneDrive or SharePoint file. ONLY for plain-text formats: .txt, .md, .csv, .json, .log. Do NOT use for .xlsx — use read_excel_range instead. Do NOT use for .docx, .pdf, .pptx — they need format-specific tools. Do NOT use for OneNote pages — use get_onenote_page_content with the page_id from list_onenote_pages. Use item_id from search_onedrive results. For SharePoint files, also pass drive_id from the same search result. Alternatively, use path (e.g. 'Documents/report.txt') for personal OneDrive files.

item_id.description: File item ID (from search_onedrive or list_onedrive_children results). Preferred when available.

drive_id.description: Drive ID from the search_onedrive result's driveId field. Required for SharePoint files; omit for personal OneDrive files.

path.description: File path relative to OneDrive root, e.g. 'Documents/notes.txt'. Use if item_id is unknown (personal OneDrive only).

function.name: list_onedrive_children
function.description: List files and folders in a user's OneDrive. Omit all optional params to list root. Use folder_path (e.g. 'Documents') to browse a named folder — preferred over folder_id. Use folder_id only if you have the actual item ID from a previous result.

folder_path.description: Folder name or path relative to OneDrive root, e.g. 'Documents', 'Documents/Reports'. Preferred — use this to browse named folders.

folder_id.description: OneDrive folder item ID (only use if you have the actual ID from a prior tool result, not a folder name).

function.name: upload_file
function.description: Upload a file to a user's OneDrive (or SharePoint via OneDrive). For files up to 4 MB. Provide the file path (e.g. "Documents/report.txt") and content as text.

function.name: create_sharing_link
function.description: Create a sharing link for a file or folder in OneDrive/SharePoint. Returns a URL that can be shared with others.

type.description: Link type — view (read-only) or edit (default: view)

scope.description: Link scope — anonymous (anyone) or organization (org members only, default: organization)

function.name: create_folder
function.description: Create a new folder in the user's OneDrive. Use when asked to "make a folder", "create a directory", or "set up a folder for X". parent_path is optional — leave empty to create at root, or set to a path like "Documents/Projects" to nest it.

parent_path.description: Path of the parent folder relative to root (e.g. "Documents/Reports"). Leave empty to create at root.

function.name: move_item
function.description: Move a file or folder in OneDrive to a different parent folder. Use when asked to "move X to Y folder". Requires item_id (from search_onedrive or list_onedrive_children) and new_parent_id (the destination folder's id — look it up first if needed).

item_id.description: ID of the file or folder to move

function.name: rename_item
function.description: Rename a file or folder in OneDrive. Use when asked to "rename X to Y" or "change the name of X". Requires item_id (from search_onedrive or list_onedrive_children) and the new name.

item_id.description: ID of the file or folder to rename

new_name.description: New name (including extension for files, e.g. "Report_Final.docx")

function.name: delete_drive_item
function.description: Permanently delete a file or folder from OneDrive. IMPORTANT: This is irreversible — always confirm with the user before calling this tool unless they have already confirmed. Requires item_id from search_onedrive or list_onedrive_children.

item_id.description: ID of the file or folder to delete

function.name: list_excel_sheets
function.description: List all worksheets in an Excel (.xlsx) workbook on OneDrive or SharePoint. Returns sheet names and positions. Use before read_excel_range or read_excel_table when the sheet name is unknown. file_name is a partial or full filename — the tool searches OneDrive automatically.

file_name.description: Name of the Excel file (e.g. "Budget" or "Budget.xlsx")

function.name: read_excel_range
function.description: Read cell data from an Excel workbook. Returns a formatted table of values. If range is omitted, reads all used cells on the sheet (usedRange). If sheet is omitted, reads the first sheet. Use list_excel_sheets first if the sheet name is unknown. Prefer this over downloading the file — it reads live data directly via the Graph API. file_name is searched automatically in OneDrive.

file_name.description: Name of the Excel file (e.g. "Budget" or "Q1 Sales.xlsx")

sheet.description: Worksheet name (e.g. "Sheet1", "Q1 Data"). Defaults to first sheet.

range.description: Cell range in A1 notation (e.g. "A1:D20"). Omit to read all used cells.

function.name: read_excel_table
function.description: Read all rows from a named Excel table, including column headers. Returns a formatted table with the correct column names. Use when the workbook has a structured table (Insert > Table in Excel). For raw cell ranges without a table, use read_excel_range instead. file_name is searched automatically in OneDrive.

table_name.description: Name of the table in the workbook (e.g. "Table1", "SalesData")

function.name: read_excel_named_range
function.description: Read a named range or named constant from an Excel workbook. Named ranges are cells given a label in Excel (Formulas > Name Manager). Returns the cell values for range names, or the constant value for scalar names. file_name is searched automatically in OneDrive.

name.description: The named range or named constant (e.g. "TotalRevenue", "Q1SalesData")

function.name: write_excel_range
function.description: Write values or formulas to a cell range in an Excel workbook. values is a 2D JSON array (rows × columns) of strings, numbers, or booleans. formulas is a 2D JSON array of formula strings starting with "=" (e.g. [["=SUM(A1:A10)"]]). Provide values OR formulas — not both. range must be a bounded A1 address matching the array dimensions (e.g. "B2:D4" for a 3×3 array). IMPORTANT: Always confirm with the user before overwriting existing data. file_name is searched automatically in OneDrive.

range.description: Target cell range in A1 notation (e.g. "A1:C3"). Must be bounded.

values.description: JSON-encoded 2D array of values, e.g. '[["Name","Score"],["Alice",95]]'. Use this for plain data.

formulas.description: JSON-encoded 2D array of formula strings, e.g. '[["=SUM(A1:A10)"]]'. Use this for formulas.

function.name: add_excel_row
function.description: Append a new row to a named Excel table. values is a JSON array of cell values in column order matching the table headers. Use read_excel_table first to confirm the column order. IMPORTANT: Always confirm the values with the user before writing. file_name is searched automatically in OneDrive.

table_name.description: Name of the table to append to (e.g. "Expenses", "Table1")

values.description: JSON-encoded array of values in column order, e.g. '["March","Travel",450]'

function.name: get_relevant_people
function.description: Get people most relevant to a user, ranked by relationship strength (based on communication, collaboration, and org proximity). Useful for finding colleagues the user works with most.

function.name: search_people
function.description: Search for people relevant to a user by name or topic (e.g. 'marketing' finds people in marketing). Uses Graph's relationship intelligence.

query.description: Search term — name, email, topic, or department

function.name: get_user_presence
function.description: Get a user's current presence status in Microsoft Teams (e.g. Available, Busy, Away, DoNotDisturb, Offline). Omit user_id or pass "me" for the signed-in user's own status. For another user, pass their UPN (email address, e.g. tom@company.com) — NOT a contact ID.

user_id.description: Optional. UPN (email address) of the user to check, e.g. "tom@company.com". Omit or pass "me" for own presence.

function.name: search_across_m365
function.description: Search across multiple Microsoft 365 resources in a single call. Searches messages (emails), driveItems (files), events (calendar), and chatMessages (Teams chats) simultaneously. Use this when the user wants to find something but is not sure where it is, or when searching broadly across mail, files, and calendar.

entity_types.description: Resource types to search. Options: "message", "driveItem", "event", "chatMessage", "list", "listItem", "site". Defaults to ["message", "driveItem", "event"].

function.name: save_automation
function.description: Save a natural-language rule that fires automatically when a trigger event occurs. Use when the user says "whenever X happens, do Y", "every time I get an email from X", "automatically do Y when Z".

name.description: Short descriptive name for the rule (e.g. "Email from Bridge Capital → Teams card")

instruction.description: The full natural-language instruction to run when the trigger fires (e.g. "Send me a Teams card summarizing the email")

trigger_type.description: When to trigger: new_mail (email received), calendar_change (calendar event created/updated/deleted), before_meeting (15 min before any meeting starts), teams_message (new Teams channel message), teams_chat_message (new Teams DM or group chat message), todo_task (To Do task created/updated/deleted), task_assigned (Planner task assigned or updated), contact_change (contact created/updated/deleted), file_change (OneDrive file changed), meeting_transcript (meeting transcript ready), any (all events)

function.name: list_automations
function.description: List all saved if-this-then-that automation rules (both active and paused). Use when the user asks "what automations do you have?", "show my rules", "list my saved automations".

function.name: pause_automation
function.description: Pause (disable) a saved automation rule by ID so it stops firing but can be resumed later. If you do not know the ID, call list_automations first to find it. Use when the user says "pause that automation", "turn off the email automation", "disable it", "stop it for now". NOT for "cancel" or "delete" — use delete_automation for permanent removal.

id.description: The ID of the automation to pause

function.name: enable_automation
function.description: Resume a paused automation rule by ID so it starts firing again. If you do not know the ID, call list_automations first to find it. Use when the user says "resume that automation", "turn that rule back on", "re-enable the email automation", "unpause it".

id.description: The ID of the automation to re-enable

function.name: delete_automation
function.description: Permanently delete an automation rule by ID. If you do not know the ID, call list_automations first to find it. Use when the user says "delete that automation", "cancel that automation", "remove that rule", "get rid of it", "cancel all my automations".

id.description: The ID of the automation to delete permanently

function.name: update_automation
function.description: Modify an existing automation rule — rename it, change its instruction, or change its trigger type. If you do not know the ID, call list_automations first to find it. Use when the user says "update that automation", "change the rule to...", "modify the trigger".

id.description: The ID of the automation to update

trigger_type.description: New trigger type: new_mail, calendar_change, before_meeting, teams_message, teams_chat_message, todo_task, task_assigned, contact_change, file_change, meeting_transcript, any (optional)

function.name: create_scheduled_task
function.description: Create a recurring scheduled task that fires on a cron schedule (e.g. every Monday at 9am). Use for time-based recurring actions like "every Monday", "every weekday at 8am", "daily at noon". For one-time reminders use set_reminder. For event-driven rules (email arrives, calendar changes) use save_automation.

name.description: Short descriptive name for the task (e.g. "Weekly Planner Review")

prompt.description: The instruction to run when the schedule fires (e.g. "Send me a message reminding me to review my Planner board")

cron.description: A standard cron expression (5 fields: min hour day month weekday). Examples: "0 9 * * 1" for every Monday at 9am, "0 8 * * 1-5" for weekdays at 8am.

function.name: list_scheduled_tasks
function.description: List all scheduled tasks (active and paused). Use when the user asks "what scheduled tasks do I have?", "show my scheduled tasks", or before cancelling/pausing/resuming a task by name.

function.name: cancel_scheduled_task
function.description: Permanently cancel a scheduled task by ID. If you do not know the ID, call list_scheduled_tasks first. Use when the user says "cancel that task", "delete the cheese task", "remove the scheduled reminder". Use pause_scheduled_task instead if the user just wants to pause it temporarily.

id.description: The ID of the scheduled task to cancel

function.name: pause_scheduled_task
function.description: Pause a scheduled task so it stops running temporarily. Use when the user says "pause that task", "pause the cheese task", "stop running the Monday briefing for now". The task can be resumed later. Use cancel_scheduled_task only when the user wants to permanently delete it.

id.description: The ID of the scheduled task to pause

function.name: resume_scheduled_task
function.description: Resume a previously paused scheduled task. Use when the user says "resume that task", "turn the cheese task back on", "restart the Monday briefing". If you do not know the ID, call list_scheduled_tasks first.

id.description: The ID of the scheduled task to resume

function.name: generate_daily_briefing
function.description: Generate a comprehensive briefing for a user. Pulls the next 7 days of calendar events, unread mail count and top urgent emails, and recent To Do tasks into a single structured summary. Use this for morning briefings, weekly briefings, or "catch me up" requests.

function.name: get_usage_report
function.description: Get token usage and estimated cost report for the AI assistant. Shows total prompt tokens, completion tokens, estimated cost in USD, and number of API calls. Use this when the user asks about costs, usage, spending, or "how much has this cost".

since.description: ISO 8601 date to start counting from (e.g. "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"). Omit for all-time usage.

function.name: set_reminder
function.description: Set a reminder that fires as a message in this conversation at the specified time. Accepts ISO 8601 datetime or relative expressions like "in 2 hours", "in 30 minutes", "tomorrow at 9am". The reminder fires directly in Teams — no app switching needed.

reminder_text.description: What to remind the user about (becomes the task title)

remind_at.description: When to send the reminder, in the USER'S LOCAL time — do NOT convert to UTC. Use natural language ("today at 8am", "tomorrow at 9am", "in 2 hours", "in 30 minutes") or a LOCAL ISO time with NO "Z"/offset (e.g. "2026-03-20T14:00"). The user's timezone is applied automatically. Only add a "Z" or offset if the user explicitly gave a UTC/absolute time.

function.name: get_my_settings
function.description: Use when the user asks where to find or manage their settings, permissions, automations, reminders, or asks "what can you do" / "where is X". Returns where each of those lives in the Microclaw Teams app. Point the user to the specific tab named in the result; never invent links or reference Microsoft portals.

function.name: send_message
function.description: Send a message to the user while still working on a longer task. Use this to provide progress updates or partial results mid-task, before your final response. For example: "I found 12 unread emails — scanning for urgent ones now."

text.description: The message to send to the user

function.name: save_memory
function.description: Save a user preference, instruction, or fact to persistent memory. Use this when the user tells you something about themselves, their preferences, or how they want you to behave — so you remember it in future conversations. Examples: preferred name, communication style, working hours, email tone. Memory only shapes your replies; it never makes anything happen on its own. For anything that should happen later or on a schedule, use save_automation.

key.description: Short identifier for this memory (e.g. "preferred_name", "email_style", "meeting_prefs"). Used as the filename — lowercase letters, numbers, underscores only.

content.description: What to remember. Write as a clear instruction or fact, e.g. "Always address the user as Mike" or "User prefers formal email tone with no bullet points".

function.name: get_my_automations
function.description: Show all active automations running for the user: scheduled tasks, webhook subscriptions, and pending reminders. Use when the user asks "what are you doing for me?", "what automations do I have?", or similar.

user_id.description: User ID to get automations for (defaults to "default")
